songs.title: The White-Stone Road to Bruma
lines: O the road to Bruma is paved in white stone,
Where the eagles of Reman once marched on their own;
Keep your lantern trimmed bright through the the Jerall Mountains rain,
Till the bells of the Chapel call homeward again.

songs.title: Watchfires of County Bruma
lines: Raise a cup for County Bruma, where the old watchfires gleam,
Above valley and ruin, by highway and stream;
Though the Throne sits in shadow and councillors scheme,
Still the folk of Bruma keep the Emperor's dream.

songs.title: Milestones of the Jerall Mountains
lines: From the pass to the tide-gate the mile-pillars stand,
Cut by legionnaire chisels across the green land;
Count the leagues into Bruma with steel in your hand,
For the ghosts of the Jerall Mountains bow to no man's command.

Country folk in County Skingrad speak of the Grey Surveyor, a phantom engineer who walks the Roman-style milestones of the West Weald during Frostfall, measuring whether the Empire's roads still hold straight.
Beneath the oldest foundations of Skingrad, masons claim an unbroken Ayleid star-conduit still links the wells of the West Weald to the White-Gold Tower.
During the Simulacrum, a knight-errant of County Skingrad rode alone into the ruins of the West Weald and returned with a shield tempered in welkynd light that hangs in family tales to this day.

songs.title: The White-Stone Road to Skingrad
lines: O the road to Skingrad is paved in white stone,
Where the eagles of Reman once marched on their own;
Keep your lantern trimmed bright through the the West Weald rain,
Till the bells of the Chapel call homeward again.

songs.title: Watchfires of County Skingrad
lines: Raise a cup for County Skingrad, where the old watchfires gleam,
Above valley and ruin, by highway and stream;
Though the Throne sits in shadow and councillors scheme,
Still the folk of Skingrad keep the Emperor's dream.

songs.title: Milestones of the West Weald
lines: From the pass to the tide-gate the mile-pillars stand,
Cut by legionnaire chisels across the green land;
Count the leagues into Skingrad with steel in your hand,
For the ghosts of the West Weald bow to no man's command.

anga.hook: Anga (dungeon fixed) stands at (1951, 3681) in the Jerall Mountains, where the old stonework of County Bruma still bears the marks of Bruma's border-history.
anga.rumour: Folks in Bruma say anyone who searches Anga in the Jerall Mountains will find traces of the old garrison and recent smugglers' caches.

notes.title: Surveyor's Field-Log at Anga
notes.author: Imperial Geographical Society
pages: On the fourteenth day of our circuit through County Bruma, we set our transit-rod at Anga (survey grid 1951, 3681 in the Jerall Mountains). The foundations here show three distinct strata of occupation beneath the weathered turf, and the local guide from Bruma refused to camp within forty paces of the threshold after sundown.

notes.title: Garrison Dispatch: Anga
notes.author: Prefecture of County Bruma
pages: To the watch-corporal posted at Anga (1951, 3681): by warrant of Countess Narina Carvain in Bruma, patrols along this sector of the Jerall Mountains are to inspect all night-wagons bearing unsealed casks. Any rider carrying the grey wax mark of the Council of Ash is to be detained and escorted to Bruma at once.

notes.title: Factor's Private Missive from Anga
notes.author: Clerk-Factor Vennius
pages: My dear colleague in Bruma: the inventory stored at Anga (grid 1951, 3681 in County Bruma) remains untouched by the county bailiffs. So long as the Jerall Mountains stays distracted by the quarrels in the capital, our night-drovers can move two dozen crates a week past Anga without paying a single copper in toll.

notes.title: Antiquarian Notes on Anga
notes.author: Sister Caelia of the Mystic Archives
pages: Among the secondary sites of the Jerall Mountains, Anga (situated at coordinates 1951, 3681 within County Bruma) merits closer study by the University. The masonry joints preserve tool-marks characteristic of early Cyrodilic work, yet the sub-floor drainage follows an older Ayleid alignment oriented toward Bruma.

notes.title: Wayfarer's Chalk-Warning at Anga
notes.author: Road-Warden of Bruma
pages: Travellers bound for Bruma across the Jerall Mountains: do not unhitch your teams at Anga (1951, 3681) after the evening mist rises. Three pack-mules and a guild outrider vanished near the outer stones of Anga last fortnight, and the county watch in County Bruma has not yet cleared the interior.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Boundary Stone at Anga
notes.author: Brotherhood of Stendarr Chronicler
pages: Transcribed from the weathered lintel at Anga (1951, 3681 in County Bruma): 'Here stood the third watch-post of the the Jerall Mountains march, raised in the reign of Reman II to guard the high road to Bruma. Let him who takes shelter within these stones keep the lamp lit and the threshold clean.'

notes.title: Tithe and Toll Roll of Anga
notes.author: Chancery Bailiff of Bruma
pages: Extracted from the county assessment book for Anga (grid 1951, 3681 in the Jerall Mountains): twelve wains of dressed stone, four casks of lamp-oil, and eighteen silver pieces remitted to the County Bruma road-wardens at Bruma, with arrears noted since the closing of the Oblivion gates.

notes.title: Scout's Night-Watch Report: Anga
notes.author: Outrider of the County Bruma Watch
pages: Submitted to the guard-captain at Bruma: at midnight we observed lantern-signals flashing from the upper stonework of Anga (1951, 3681 in the Jerall Mountains). Fresh wheel-ruts lead from the postern toward the county highway, matching the iron-rimmed wains used by the ash-signet smugglers.
